components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, here backing away
艮 (gèn) gives only a loose sound hint for tuì

example.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng hòu tuì yí bù.
example.english: Please take one step back.
example.fact: 退 goes beyond retreating to "giving back": 退钱 (refund), 退货 (return goods), 退票 (return a ticket). 退休 means to retire from work, and 后退 means to move backwards.

components.note: 冃 (mào) is an old character for a hat and supplies the sound
目 (eye) — a hat pulled down over the eyes, the old picture of covering

example.pinyin: Bēizi lǐ mào zhe rèqì.
example.english: Steam is rising from the cup.
example.fact: 冒 means to rise or emerge: 冒烟 (give off smoke), 冒汗 (break into a sweat). It also means to brave (冒险, adventure) or to fake (冒牌, counterfeit), and 感冒 is the ordinary word for a cold.

components.note: Old form is usually read as an arrow landing on a line, the ground, hence 'to arrive'

example.hanzi: 从早上八点至晚上六点营业。
example.pinyin: Cóng zǎoshang bā diǎn zhì wǎnshang liù diǎn yíngyè.
example.english: Open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
example.fact: 至 is the formal counterpart of 到 for "to / until", common on signs and schedules. It also builds 至少 (at least), 至今 (until now), 甚至 (even) and 至于 (as for).

components.note: 钅 (metal) — a metal weight pressing something down
真 (zhēn) gives the sound; zhèn is a near match

example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozhèn hěn ānjìng.
example.english: This little town is very quiet.
example.fact: 镇 began as pressing down with a weight; the "town" meaning came from a garrison holding an area. It is now the administrative level 乡镇, and also forms 镇静 (calm) and 冰镇 (chilled with ice).

components.note: 丬 (jiāng/qiáng) is a remnant of 將 in the old 獎 and supplies the sound
大 replaces the dog radical of old 獎; it is a graphic simplification

example.pinyin: Tā dé le yí ge dà jiǎng.
example.english: He won a big prize.
example.fact: 奖 is a prize and also to reward: 奖励 (reward), 奖学金 (scholarship), 中奖 (to win a lottery prize) and 夸奖 (to praise). 诺贝尔奖 is the Nobel Prize.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雇 was first the name of a kind of bird, and the meaning of 'hire' came by borrowing
户 (hù) gives a rough sound hint for gù

example.pinyin: Tāmen gù le yí ge sījī.
example.english: They hired a driver.
example.fact: 雇 means to hire someone for pay, and 雇主 is the employer. It is used for hiring labour such as drivers, helpers and cleaners; for formal staff appointments Chinese uses 聘 instead.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — two drops, the ice radical
水 (water) — water that has frozen

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi bīngshuǐ.
example.english: Please give me a glass of iced water.
example.fact: 冰 stands for both ice and iced drinks: 冰咖啡, 冰淇淋 (ice cream). Many Chinese people prefer hot or warm drinks, so asking for 冰水 can feel unusual. 冰箱 is the refrigerator and 冰山 an iceberg.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water flowing through a hollow
同 (tóng) gives the sound; dòng is close

example.pinyin: Qiáng shang yǒu yí ge dòng.
example.english: There is a hole in the wall.
example.fact: 洞 is also the radio and military spoken form of the digit 0, when numbers must not be confused: 洞 (0), 幺 (1), 拐 (7). It forms 山洞 (cave), 洞穴 (cavern) and 黑洞 (black hole).

components.note: Origin is uncertain; in modern writing it works as a literary word meaning 'if' or 'like'

example.pinyin: Ruò yǒu wèntí, qǐng gàosu wǒ.
example.english: If you have any problem, please tell me.
example.fact: 若 is the written-style "if", more formal than 如果; you will see it on notices and in literature. It also appears in 若干 (several), 若无其事 (as if nothing had happened) and 假若 (supposing).

components.note: 刂 (knife) — rules were engraved with a blade
贝 (shell) is a simplified stand-in for the vessel on which the old 則 shows rules being carved

example.hanzi: 他喜欢甜的，我则喜欢咸的。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tián de, wǒ zé xǐhuan xián de.
example.english: He likes sweet, whereas I like salty.
example.fact: As a conjunction 则 contrasts or follows on: "whereas", "then". As a noun it is a rule: 规则, 原则, and 否则 means "otherwise". It is also a measure word for items of news or short texts: 一则新闻.

components.note: Simplified form of 應; the 广 and the rest are a graphic reduction, not a clue to sound or meaning

example.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
example.english: You should rest earlier.
example.fact: 应 is read yīng in 应该 and 应当 (should), but yìng for "to respond" in 回应 and 应用 (to apply). 答应 (dāying, to promise) has a neutral second syllable.

components.note: 饣 (food) — a food item
并 (bìng) gives the sound; bǐng is close

example.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen chī yuèbǐng.
example.english: We eat mooncakes at the Mid-Autumn Festival.
example.fact: 饼 covers any flat round food, not just sweet ones: 月饼 (mooncake), 煎饼 (thin savoury pancake), 烧饼 (sesame flatbread). 饼干 is a biscuit or cracker.

components.note: 亻 (person) — originally a person carrying a load, the word later borrowed for 'what'
可 (kě) gives the sound; hé is close

example.pinyin: Nǐ wèi hé bù lái?
example.english: Why aren't you coming?
example.fact: 何 is the literary question word, which appears in modern Chinese only in set words: 如何 (how), 为何 (why), 任何 (any), 何必 (why bother), 何时 (when). In speech 什么 replaces it.

components.note: Simplified form of 電, which showed lightning streaking under a rain cloud; the modern shape keeps just the streak

example.pinyin: Shǒujī méi diàn le.
example.english: The phone has run out of battery.
example.fact: 电 originally meant lightning, and it became the root of nearly every modern technology word: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电影, 电梯. 没电 means out of battery or power.

components.note: A number character; its shape is a mark added to a base form, not a picture of an object

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu yì qiān yè.
example.english: This book has a thousand pages.
example.fact: Chinese counts in 万 (ten thousands), so 千 is always one level below that: 一万 = ten 千. 千万 means "ten million" as a number and "by all means" in warnings, as in 千万别忘了 (don't forget!).

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — fabric
The upper part is a worn-down older 父 (fù), giving a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā yòng bù zuò le yí ge bāo.
example.english: She made a bag out of cloth.
example.fact: 布 originally meant plain cloth (of cotton or hemp), in contrast to fancy silk, and later extended to spreading or announcing: 发布 (to release), 公布 (to publish), 布置 (to arrange).

meanings: used in place names and transliterations

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洛 was a river name
各 (gè) gives a rough sound hint for luò

example.pinyin: Tāmen qù le Luòshānjī.
example.english: They went to Los Angeles.
example.fact: 洛 names the Luo River in Henan, around which the ancient capital 洛阳 (Luoyang) grew up. Today it appears mostly in transliterations such as 洛杉矶 (Los Angeles).

excludeSuggestion: Mostly occurs in place names and transliterated names

components.note: 亻 (person) — originally a group of ten people
十 (ten) — the number ten

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài kàn shénme?
example.english: What are you looking at?
example.fact: In everyday speech 什 appears almost only inside 什么 (what). The word 什么 can be indefinite too: 有什么问题吗 (are there any problems?). 为什么 is "why". 什 as a number word (shí) is rare and old.

components.note: 米 (rice) — a food ingredient
唐 (táng) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Tā bù chī tài duō táng.
example.english: She doesn't eat too much sugar.
example.fact: 糖 means both sugar and candy: 白糖 (white sugar), 糖果 (sweets), 棉花糖 (candy floss). Diabetes is 糖尿病, literally "sugar urine disease", and 糖葫芦 is the candied hawthorn skewer.

components.note: Simplified form of 舊; the 丨日 shape replaces the old bird-and-mortar shape and carries no clue to sound or meaning

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài jiù le.
example.english: This garment is too old.
example.fact: 旧 is the opposite of 新 and refers to things worn with age (旧书, 旧衣服). 老 is for living beings or long-standing things. 念旧 means sentimental about the past and 怀旧 means nostalgic.

components.note: Simplified form of 靈 (with a rain radical and shamans); the modern top-and-fire shape is a graphic reduction

example.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn líng.
example.english: This method works really well.
example.fact: 灵 as a spoken adjective means effective, said of remedies or tricks: 很灵. It forms 灵活 (flexible), 灵感 (inspiration), 心灵 (mind, spirit) and 灵魂 (soul).

components.note: 舟 (boat) — originally linked with moving a boat
殳 (a hand holding a tool) — pushing it along

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng háizi yìbān gāoxìng.
example.english: He is happy like a child.
example.fact: 般 is nearly always inside 一般 (ordinary, usually). It also marks similes with 如 / 像 ... 般, as in 雪一般白 (white as snow) and 如梦般 (dreamlike).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — control is a hand gesture
空 (kōng) gives the sound; kòng is close

example.hanzi: 他控制不了自己的脾气。
example.pinyin: Tā kòngzhì bu liǎo zìjǐ de píqi.
example.english: He can't control his temper.
example.fact: 控 appears in 控制 (control), 遥控 (remote control) and 控告 (to accuse). In recent slang it is a suffix for "fan of": 颜控 is someone obsessed with good looks, borrowed from the Japanese コン.

components.note: 走 (walk) — a trip made on foot
尚 (shàng) gives a loose sound hint for tàng

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù le yí tàng Běijīng.
example.english: I made a trip to Beijing.
example.fact: 趟 counts a trip there and back: 去一趟, 跑一趟. It also counts scheduled runs of trains or buses: 这趟火车 (this train service). It differs from 次, which counts any occasion.

components.note: 毛 (fur) — fur on the outside
衣 (clothing) — fur worn on the outer side of a garment, hence 'outer surface, to show'

example.pinyin: Qǐng tián yíxià zhè zhāng biǎo.
example.english: Please fill in this form.
example.fact: In simplified writing 表 merges several old characters: surface (表面), form (表格), a watch (手表) and "to show" (表示). 表哥 and 表妹 are cousins through the mother or sisters, not the father's side.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a boundary on all sides
木 (tree) — a tree boxed in, the picture of being trapped

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn kùn, xiǎng shuìjiào.
example.english: I am sleepy and want to sleep.
example.fact: In daily speech 困 mostly means "sleepy", whereas 累 means "tired"; 我很困 is about wanting to sleep. In writing it means trapped or in hardship: 被困 (trapped) and 困难 (difficulty).

components.note: Simplified form of 喬; the lower part is a reduction and does not map to meaning or sound

example.pinyin: Tā xìng Qiáo.
example.english: His surname is Qiao.
example.fact: 乔 is a surname, and 乔迁 (to move to a new, better home) is the congratulatory expression for moving house, as in 乔迁之喜. On its own the meaning "tall" is bookish.

excludeSuggestion: Almost only used as a surname and in 乔迁/乔装

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 物 first named cattle of varied colours, then things in general
勿 (wù) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí jiàn hěn guì de lǐwù.
example.english: This is a very expensive gift.
example.fact: 物 is a bound form meaning thing: 礼物 (gift), 动物, 植物, 食物, 物价 (prices), 物理 (physics). For "thing" in speech Chinese uses 东西; 物 is the written-register counterpart.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — money and trade
化 (huà) gives the sound; huò is close

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de huò hěn xīn.
example.english: This shop's stock is very new.
example.fact: 货 means goods to be bought or sold: 送货 (to deliver), 进货 (to restock), 货币 (currency). As slang it is an insult, as in 蠢货 (idiot) or 你这个货.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a liquid
由 (yóu) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào fàng tài duō yóu.
example.english: Please don't put in too much oil.
example.fact: 油 covers cooking oil (食用油), petrol (汽油) and crude oil (石油). 加油 literally means to add oil, so it is both what you do at a petrol station and the cheer "go for it!".

components.note: A person in a sitting or lying posture, which in this form is read as a corpse; as a radical it often just means 'body'

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá fāxiàn le yí jù shītǐ.
example.english: The police found a body.
example.fact: 尸 is nearly always used in 尸体 (corpse); the measure word for corpses is 具. The same shape is also a common radical on top of characters like 屋 (house) and 层 (storey), where it has little to do with corpses.

components.note: 能 (néng) was originally a drawing of a bear; later borrowed to mean 'able'
灬 (fire dots) were added under it to give a new character for the animal

example.pinyin: Xióng xǐhuan chī fēngmì.
example.english: Bears like to eat honey.
example.fact: 熊猫 (panda) literally means "bear cat". The measure word is 只 or 头. In spoken Chinese 熊 is also slang for wimpy or useless: 你真熊 means "you are such a wimp".

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person comparing worth
直 (zhí) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū zhí wǔshí kuài qián.
example.english: This book is worth fifty yuan.
example.fact: 值 is "to be worth": 值钱 (valuable), 值得 (worth doing), 价值 (value). 值班 means to be on duty or on shift, because 值 also means "to take one's turn".

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倍 first meant to turn against or go beyond
咅 (pǒu) shares the sound loosely with bèi

example.pinyin: Tā de gōngzī shì wǒ de liǎng bèi.
example.english: His salary is twice mine.
example.fact: 倍 is a multiplier: 两倍 (twice), 三倍 (three times). With a verb like 增加, 增加了一倍 means "doubled", but 增加了两倍 is ambiguous (tripled or doubled?), so careful writers say 增加到.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — wiping is done by hand
察 (chá) gives the sound; cā is close

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi cā gānjìng.
example.english: Please wipe the table clean.
example.fact: 擦 covers wiping (擦桌子), rubbing on (擦药, apply ointment) and brushing past (擦伤, graze; 擦肩而过, to pass by each other closely). 橡皮擦 is an eraser.

components.note: The lower part is a kneeling person (㔾), usually read as someone curled up; the top part is a worn-down hand-and-grain shape. 'Roll' follows from the curled posture

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ dìtú juǎn qǐlai le.
example.english: He rolled up the map.
example.fact: 卷 is juǎn when it means to roll (卷发, curly hair) and juàn when it means a scroll, volume or exam paper (试卷). The 2020s buzzword 内卷 ("involution") means rat-race competition, also read juǎn.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — a vessel
叟 (sǒu) gives the sound; sōu is close

example.pinyin: Gǎngkǒu lǐ tíng zhe sān sōu dà chuán.
example.english: Three large ships are docked in the harbour.
example.fact: 艘 is the measure word for ships and larger vessels: 一艘轮船, 一艘航空母舰. Small boats are usually counted with 条 or 只 instead.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — hands joined together, the sense of doing something jointly

example.pinyin: Wǒmen gòng yǒu èrshí ge xuésheng.
example.english: We have twenty students in all.
example.fact: 共 as an adverb means "altogether": 一共, 共计. It forms 共同 (common, joint), 共享 (to share) and 共和国 (republic). The party name 共产党 means "common-property party".

components.note: 刂 (knife) — piercing
朿 (cì) is a drawing of a thorn and supplies the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, méigui yǒu cì.
example.english: Be careful, the rose has thorns.
example.fact: 刺 is both the thorn and the act of stabbing: 刺伤, 刺绣 (embroidery), 刺猬 (hedgehog). 刺激 is stimulation and can be a thrill: 很刺激 means "exciting".

components.note: 火 (fire) — cooking over heat
少 (shǎo) gives a loose sound hint for chǎo

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī chǎofàn.
example.english: I want to eat fried rice.
example.fact: 炒 is the high-heat wok technique central to Chinese cooking: 炒饭, 炒面, 炒菜. It also means to speculate (炒股, to play the stock market), to hype (炒作), and 炒鱿鱼 (fire someone) because squid curls up like a bedroll when stir-fried.

components.note: Origin is debated; in modern use the character is a pure written unit for 'now'

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.
example.english: The weather is very nice today.
example.fact: 今 is a bound morpheme in time words: 今天 (today), 今年 (this year), 今晚 (tonight), 今后 (from now on). On its own it is classical: 古今 means ancient and modern.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the old 臟 was about internal organs
庄 (zhuāng) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒu tài zāng le.
example.english: Your hands are too dirty.
example.fact: Simplified 脏 merges two old characters, 髒 (zāng, dirty) and 臟 (zàng, organs). So the same shape reads zāng in 肮脏 (filthy) but zàng in 心脏 (heart) and 内脏 (internal organs).

components.note: 亼 (jí) is a lid or gathering shape
口 (mouth) — an opening the lid fits over

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié hěn hé jiǎo.
example.english: These shoes fit well.
example.fact: 合 is about things fitting together: 合适 (suitable), 合作 (to cooperate), 合同 (contract), 合影 (group photo). As a verb it also means to close, as in 合上书 (close the book).

components.note: 大 (big) — something out of the ordinary in size
可 (kě) is thought to supply the sound; the fit with qí is loose

example.pinyin: Zhè zhēn shì yí jiàn qíguài de shì.
example.english: This is really a strange thing.
example.fact: 奇 has two readings: qí (strange: 好奇 curious, 奇迹 miracle) and jī (odd, as in 奇数, an odd number, opposite of 偶数). 奇怪 is the common spoken word for "strange".

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a sound made with the mouth
米 (mǐ) gives the sound; mī is nearly identical

example.hanzi: 我家有一只可爱的猫咪。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī kě'ài de māomī.
example.english: We have a cute kitten at home.
example.fact: 咪 imitates the sound of a cat and is nearly always seen in 猫咪, an affectionate word for a pet cat. Calling a cat is 咪咪 (mīmī). Don't confuse it with 眯 (mī, to squint).

components.note: 纟 (silk) — early paper fibres were silk-related
氏 (shì) gives a loose sound hint for zhǐ

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng zhǐ.
example.english: Please give me a sheet of paper.
example.fact: Paper (造纸术) is one of China's Four Great Inventions, traditionally credited to the court official 蔡伦 around AD 105, though older paper has been found. The measure word is 张: 一张纸. 报纸 is a newspaper.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain being weighed
尔 stands in for the older sound part of 稱; a simplification, not a sound clue

example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēng tā wéi Lǎo Wáng.
example.english: Everyone calls him Old Wang.
example.fact: 称 is chēng in 称呼 (form of address), 称赞 (to praise) and 称为 (to be called). It is chèn in 相称 (to match) and 称心 (satisfying), a different word with the same character.

components.note: 马 (horse) — riding a horse
奇 (qí) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
example.english: I ride my bike to work every day.
example.fact: 骑 is the verb for straddled mounts: 骑马, 骑车, 骑摩托车. For cars and trains Chinese uses 坐 (ride as a passenger) or 开 (drive), so 骑 depends on how you sit.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — gripping, as in 'to seize, rely on'
居 (jū) gives the sound; jù is close

example.pinyin: Jùshuō míngtiān huì xià yǔ.
example.english: It is said that it will rain tomorrow.
example.fact: 据 is a bound morpheme in 根据 (according to), 数据 (data), 证据 (evidence), 据说 (it is said) and 据点 (stronghold). 据 is the written form of "according to"; the spoken equivalent is 按照.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — a slow movement
尺 (chǐ) gives the sound; chí is close

example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.
example.english: Sorry, I'm late.
example.fact: 迟 means late past an expected time: 迟到 (to arrive late), 迟早 (sooner or later), 推迟 (to postpone). 晚 is just late in the day or after a time, whereas 迟 implies a missed deadline.
